ranked_moves.title: Fail-closed `check`: read every needed job's verdict, take coverage off the required path, and put a timeout on every job
ranked_moves.why: Today a red preflight cannot block a merge: `check` runs with always() and its gate script never reads the preflight result (critic CONFIRMED, ci.yml:1903-1925; ruleset 22281319 requires only check/guards/frontend).
ranked_moves.payoff: Restores 7 advisory checks to merge-blocking; about 45-49s off both PR-full and merge_group critical paths (check p50 54s to about 5-8s, measured from the push-event check); caps hang cost at about 2x p95 (one incident cost about 340 runner-min).
ranked_moves.outcome: The required `check` gate fails whenever any job it needs fails, is cancelled or skips outside a table of allowed cases; check-preflight's lint, format, lock, SQL-safety, exact-once, budget and smoke verdicts become merge-blocking; coverage combine and badge move to a non-required merge_group job; every CI job and test has a timeout derived from its p95.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No change to which tests run; no coverage threshold introduced; no new required check names (the ruleset keeps check/guards/frontend).
ranked_moves.governing_intent: about/craft-and-care/engineering-bar.md (fail-closed default bar); about/craft-and-care/testing-and-verification.md Evidence Expectations; ci.yml:1903-1953 comment states the intent that a failed preflight fails `check`, which `if: always()` defeats.

ranked_moves.title: Stop stale-branch push storms: prune merged and stale remote branches, delete branches on merge, and clear branch-scoped caches
ranked_moves.why: A 2026-10-03 storm queued about 1,515 junk runs and starved the runner pool (worst PR waited 5h50m against a 12.8 min p50); the 10 GB cache budget is 99% non-main refs, so PR `npm ci` misses the cache.
ranked_moves.payoff: Removes the measured multi-hour runner-starvation class; restores cache hits; saves about 39 min per session-link body fix (4 in two weeks).
ranked_moves.outcome: Merged and abandoned remote branches are pruned; delete-branch-on-merge is on; Actions caches from non-main refs no longer evict the main-scoped npm and uv caches; the session-link guard reads the live PR body so a body fix does not need an empty commit.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No deletion of branches with open PRs or unmerged commits newer than the stated horizon; no change to required checks.
ranked_moves.governing_intent: about/craft-and-care/engineering-bar.md Change Hygiene; repo-now-uses-github-merge-queue and session-link-guard memories (the guard reads the frozen event payload today).
ranked_moves.surface_map:
Repo setting delete_branch_on_merge=true; a one-off owner-approved prune of branches whose PR is merged or closed (agent/*, qa/*, fix/*, codex/*); `gh cache delete` for non-main node-cache entries; the butlers-tooling QA-PR workflow that creates qa/* branches (it must branch from current origin/main); AGENTS.md session-completion cleanup step.

Rollback: closed PRs keep refs/pull/N/head, so a deleted branch can be restored from its PR. Idempotent: rerunning the prune on an already-clean set is a no-op. Deletion is destructive, so the owner must approve the branch list.
Assurance: No test or guard is removed. Branch deletion drops only refs whose PRs are merged or closed, and their code survives in main or in PR refs.
ranked_moves.verification:
`gh api repos/tzeusy-org/butlers/branches --paginate | jq length` drops from about 2,000; `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --event push` shows only main for 14 days; `gh api .../actions/cache/usage` is under 10 GB with a refs/heads/main node-cache entry present.

ranked_moves.title: Fail before CI, react at the first red shard: an enforced pre-push hook for tree-deterministic guards, the session-link fix at the source, and a red-run reaction kit
ranked_moves.why: 10 of 60 failed PR runs in two weeks were static, tree-deterministic failures CI could have been spared; red PRs lose about 12.5 min each to late reaction and repeat cycles of 21-25 min.
ranked_moves.payoff: About 10 red PR runs per two weeks avoided; about 200 agent-minutes per 45 PRs from earlier reaction; about 2.6 h of PR lead time per fortnight from the session-link class.
ranked_moves.outcome: An enforced pre-push hook runs the deterministic static guards (openspec strict, format, manifests or partition check, budget, session-link scan over commit messages); the harness attribution no longer writes a session URL that the guard rejects; workers react at the first failing shard with a complete failing-node digest and reproduce locally before re-pushing.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No hook that runs tests or needs a DB; the hook never replaces the CI guard; no bypass flag in agent guidance.
ranked_moves.governing_intent: about/craft-and-care/engineering-bar.md Definition of Done; AGENTS.md 'Cheap standing pre-push checks' (documented but unenforced).

findings.detail: No bytecode or venv cache: ci.yml has no actions/cache or UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE, and each of the 11 jobs runs uv sync --frozen (14-22 s) and compiles .pyc cold.

findings.title: Root conftest eagerly imports torch/sentence_transformers in every pytest process
findings.evidence: conftest.py:105 _default_registry() pulls in approvals/module, then decision_memory, then memory/storage.py:61 _load_module('embedding'), then embedding.py:9 'from sentence_transformers import'; that is 4.27 s warm / 11.78 s cold of the 7.85 s conftest import; memory/__init__.py:878 already says th…
findings.detail: The cost is paid by the controller, each xdist worker, every one of the 14 preflight collection subprocesses, and every local agent `uv run pytest` (44% of the 10.7 s fixed startup). storage.py also re-executes embedding.py via spec_from_file_location, creating a duplicate module copy.

findings.title: Legacy postgres:16 service container started in 11 jobs while tests use testcontainers pgvector:pg17
findings.evidence: ci.yml services.postgres image postgres:16 appears 12 times (added in the Feb skeleton, bc7035284); conftest.py:552 uses PostgresContainer('pgvector/pgvector:pg17'); 'Initialize containers' takes 22-24 s p50 per job; tests/contracts/test_ci_test_targets.py:339-341 pins the shape
findings.detail: I could not prove it is unused, because src/butlers/db.py:322 reads DATABASE_URL and 24 tests patch it, so it needs one A/B run. It is also the wrong major version (16 vs pg17 in production).

findings.title: PR shards wait for a separate `plan` job that runs a stdlib-only planner after a full uv sync
findings.evidence: plan p50 31 s (uv sync 17 s); PR shards end at about 742 s vs 697 s for merge_group; scoped_runner, changed_files and source_test_map import only stdlib (imports fine on system python3)
findings.detail: This adds about 34 s to every backend PR critical path and one extra job per PR run against the 20-job cap.

findings.title: Adding a test file forces the PR off the scoped lane
findings.evidence: Only 2/19 backend PRs ran scoped; 3/14 sampled plan logs escalated with "'.github/ci-test-shards/unit-5.txt' matches shared-infrastructure pattern '.github/'"
findings.detail: Every new test file needs a manifest edit, and that edit triggers the .github/ escalation, so test-adding PRs pay the full matrix (807 s vs 476 s).

findings.title: Runner performance is bimodal, so max-of-11 parallel jobs nearly always hits a slow runner
findings.evidence: merge_group unit-1 test step 246-434 s and preflight verify 203-310 s on the same corpus; uncorrelated across shards in the same run; same runner image 20260927.320.1
findings.detail: p95 planning must assume slow-mode throughput, about 1.6x fast mode. A runner CPU probe (lscpu) is not logged today, so the CPU-model cause is inferred, not proven.

findings.title: Free-plan concurrency cap causes job queueing on 36-40% of runs
findings.evidence: org plan=free (gh api orgs/tzeusy-org); 10/25 merge_group and 9/25 PR runs had a job queued >30 s; per-run max-queue p95 is 99 s / 187 s; a merge_group run has 17 jobs
findings.detail: Every extra shard costs queue time. Consolidating jobs (plan into changes, coverage off the path) gives capacity back. Larger runners are not available on the free plan, and bu-gvut0.5 excludes paid runners.

findings.title: About 2,075 stale remote branches can starve CI; one burst queued at least 1,000 runs for hours
findings.evidence: 2026-10-03: at least 1,000 push-event runs on distinct non-main branches (e.g. run 37151267998, branch qa/general/...), using an old ci.yml with 'on: push' and no branch filter; created-to-done p50 201 min; delete_branch_on_merge=false; 1,847 agent/* heads
findings.detail: This was a one-off incident, but the hazard is still there. Any re-push of a stale branch runs the old workflow and takes runners from the 20-job pool.

findings.title: push to main re-runs frontend and e2e on the tree merge_group already validated
findings.evidence: ci.yml:2211-2213 and 2255 run on push; push p50 frontend 445 s plus e2e 216 s; e2e-main-schedule.yml also re-runs e2e on main
findings.detail: About 11 runner-minutes per merge (about 10 merges a day) that compete with merge_group and PR runs for the cap.

Each of its 14 collection subprocesses also pays the 4.3 s sentence_transformers import from the conftest (about 60 s of the 343 s verify+budget), so the lazy-import fix speeds up preflight even before inventory reuse lands.

The profiling scope covers fixtures and migrations but not per-process fixed cost: 55-99 s of controller startup per shard (cold pyc plus eager torch import) is larger than any single fixture target it lists.

The epic's numbers are stale. CI now selects 17,501 unit and 4,921 integration cases (junit for run 37408113441; local collect 17,501/22,458). The 'lane' budget should be stated per job, including about 100-150 s of fixed setup and startup that test condensation cannot remove.
